flawed_step: The implication from 3-connected and claw-free to Hamiltonian is false.
counterexample: Let P be the Petersen graph with vertices a_i,b_i (i modulo 5) and edges a_i a_{i+1}, a_i b_i, and b_i b_{i+2}. Construct H by replacing each vertex v of P with a triangle whose three vertices correspond to the three edges incident with v; for every edge e=uv of P, join the e-vertex in u's triangle to the e-vertex in v's triangle. Thus H has 30 vertices. H is claw-free: at every vertex, two of its three neighbors lie in the same triangle and are adjacent. It is 3-connected: deleting at most two vertices leaves every replacement triangle nonempty and connected; contracting these remnants produces P with at most two edges deleted, which remains connected because the Petersen graph is 3-edge-connected. Yet H is not Hamiltonian. Any Hamiltonian cycle would use exactly two external edges at every replacement triangle; suppressing the resulting path through each triangle would yield a Hamiltonian cycle in P. The Petersen graph has none: the complement of any hypothetical Hamiltonian cycle would be a perfect matching, but every perfect matching of P has complement equal to two disjoint 5-cycles.
assessment_summary: The 30-vertex triangle expansion of the Petersen graph satisfies every hypothesis but has no Hamiltonian cycle, so the statement is false.
